title: Placements — WhiteHouse College of Business & Technology
description: WhiteHouse College of Business & Technology — Kathmandu University affiliated BIT and B.Tech Ed IT programs in Jhapa, Nepal.

blocks.h1: Career support from classroom to workplace
paras: WCBT supports students with internship preparation, employer exposure, and career guidance for the next step after graduation.

blocks.heading: How placement support works
paras: Placement support is a gradual process. Students first build academic and project foundations, then strengthen communication and workplace readiness, and finally connect with internship and career opportunities.

groups.title: Prepare
text: Students work on CVs, portfolios, communication, project documentation, and interview confidence.

groups.title: Connect
text: The college connects students with industry exposure, employer talks, visits, and internship guidance.

groups.title: Improve
text: Students use feedback from faculty, mentors, and employers to improve skills and readiness.

blocks.heading: How we prepare students
paras: Placement support starts before graduation, combining skill preparation with practical exposure.

groups.title: Profile Readiness
text: Students receive guidance on CVs, portfolios, project presentation, and interview preparation.

groups.title: Internship Support
text: The college helps students identify internship opportunities that match their skills and program pathway.

groups.title: Employer Connections
text: Industry exposure, visits, and partner conversations connect students with real workplace expectations.

groups.title: Career Mentoring
text: Faculty and advisors help students plan for employment, entrepreneurship, and further study.

blocks.heading: What students should build before placement
bullets: A clear CV that presents education, projects, skills, and activities.
A practical project or portfolio that shows problem-solving ability.
Basic workplace communication, punctuality, teamwork, and reporting habits.
Confidence explaining technical work in interviews or presentations.
Awareness of career paths in software, IT support, ed-tech, analytics, teaching, and startups.
Willingness to learn from feedback during internships, visits, and mentoring sessions.

blocks.heading: What students can expect
bullets: Employer exposure through visits, talks, and partnerships

blocks.heading: Planning your career path?
paras: Talk with the college team about internships, projects, and graduate opportunities.
